value.answer: Short-term, melatonin looks safe for most adults. Long-term safety isn't well established, though. A preliminary AHA conference abstract (not peer-reviewed yet) linked a year or more of use in people with chronic insomnia to higher heart failure rates. It can't prove cause, and some experts think poor sleep could explain it. Keeping it short-term is the usual advice, and it's worth checking with your doctor or pharmacist before starting, especially if you're older or have had low-impact fractures.
